newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES VETERAN AMBROSE STUNS AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES VETERAN AMBROSE STUNS AUSTRALIA.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Curtly Ambrose made a stunning return to form by claiming five wickets to demoralise Australia on the first day of the third test on Thursday.
The veteran pace bowler tore through the top order as West Indies dismissed Australia for 219 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground to rejuvenate their flagging morale.
West Indies, who trail 2-0 in the five-test series, were 29 for one at close of play after an absorbing day of cricket watched by almost 73,000 spectators.
Australia all-rounders Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett both scored defiant half-centuries to rally the home side after they were reduced to 27 for four before lunch.
Only the loss of opener Sherwin Campbell to fast bowler Glenn McGrath for seven just before the close marred West Indies' most productive day of the test series to date.
Ambrose, who captured a meagre three test wickets in Brisbane and Sydney at an average of 93, inflicted the early damage by removing Mark Taylor, Matthew Hayden and Mark Waugh.
"I promised the team I would take 10 wickets in the match so I'm half way there," Ambrose told reporters in a rare media interview.
He said he was motivated by the widespread criticism of his performances so far on tour.
"My team mates have never lost faith in me and that has kept me strong. We know we have to win this match," Ambrose said.
When Waugh departed for a first-ball duck, Ambrose had the outstanding figures of three for three in seven overs.
He returned late in the innings to remove wicketkeeper Ian Healy and McGrath to finish with five for 55 from 24.5 overs, the 15th time he has captured five wickets in a test innings.
West Indies opener Robert Samuels survived a testing 13 overs before the close to remain unbeaten on 10 alongside promoted number three Shivnarine Chanderpaul on 11 not out.
West Indies must win the remaining three tests to regain the Frank Worrell trophy after losing to Australia on home soil last year.
Taylor elected to bat after winning the toss but the decision soon backfired on the Australia captain, who failed with the bat to prolong a disappointing run of scores.
Steve Waugh, who missed the second test because of a groin injury, played a typically resolute innings for 58.
He added 102 runs for the fifth wicket with fellow all-rounder Greg Blewett, who scored an equally gritty 62.
